title: In the Drops: Ogio Alpha backpack, CeramicSpeed UFO wax, Sidi Aeron gravel shoes and Assos Equipe kit

In the Drops: Ogio Alpha backpack, CeramicSpeed UFO wax, Sidi Aeron gravel shoes and Assos Equipe kit

It’s Friday, the day after Thursday, when you will of course have been diligently listening to our latest Cyclist Magazine Podcast episode with journalist and author James Witts that’s all about… doping.

Not to say anyone’s doing it, but rather Will and I chat to James about his latest book, Dope, in which he examines the current doping landscape across sport, from pushing the boundaries with things like peptides (which encourage weight loss) and carbon monoxide inhalation (which encourages the production of red blood cells) to more – conjecture it must be said – nefarious practices such as microdosing in undetectable amounts or using EPO on altitude training camps.

It’s a good one, and for once cycling comes out pretty well, with numerous experts assessing it to be one of the cleanest, best policed sports globally. But I digress, as the podcast is by no means the only thing worth shouting about that’s popped up in the Cyclist digital landscape this week. On the pro front, we’re a day away from the start of the final men’s Grand Tour of the year, and we’ve got plenty of Vuelta-themed content to soak up ahead of the Spanish Grand Tour kicking off tomorrow in… Monaco (because obviously…).

Between our general GC and sprint form guides, our guide on how to watch the race and focus on the key Vuelta climbs, not to mention our own predictions for the key competitions (check back later today), we’ve got everything you need to get up to speed 24 hours before the pros do.

But enough of all that, you’re here for In the Drops, so on with the show…

Ogio Alpha 25L backpack

I am to backpacks what Imelda Marcos is to shoes, albeit without the side order of being partner to an authoritarian dictator, even if my wife can be as strict with me about my drinking. I am forever searching for the perfect one, drawn magnetically to interesting takes on pocket arrangements, slick zips and funky colours. Which is where the Ogio Alpha comes in.

This little guy ain’t so little as it looks at 25 litres in capacity, but it wears it well, being 23cm deep, 33cm wide and 51cm high, meaning it just about satisfies Easyjet carry-on criteria with a little squishing (Easyjet says no bigger than 45x36x20cm or that will be £900, thanks).

Within that is space for a 17in laptop and tablet in two padded sleeves, two front zipped pockets, internal organiser including pen holder (do you remember pens?), natty little back security pocket for a passport or wallet, two side pockets for bottles and a top fleecy lined pocket for sunglasses. Add in some cushy straps, reflective detailing, more-useful-than-they-seem side clips that are perfect for the next time you’re carrying a French baguette in one bottle pocket and a rolled-up beach tent in the other, and the only way I could be happier is if it was made from recycled materials and was available in a tonne of colours. Which it is.

The Ogio Alpha 25L also only weighs 1,042g on my sclaes, which trust me, is light, and trust me, it’s annoying when you feel a lot of the weight of your bag is your bag. Plus the zips, which feel like they couldn’t be smoother if they’d been dipped in CeramicSpeed chain wax. Which reminds me…

  • Check out the Ogio Alpha 25L backpack at ogio.com (£99)

CeramicSpeed UFO Wax Ultra Endurance Kit

Wax treatments have been around since Brazilian times, but it’s only recently that they’ve become more accessible, and by that I mean cheaper and easier to use. Now, €54 for a big plastic pot of wax beads might seem like a lot, and the need to completely strip a chain of lube first, then melt the wax then dip in the chain then wait for it to dry might seem like an expensive faff, but the reality is this: sure, cheaper lubes exist, and dripping oil onto a chain is dead easy, but CeramicSpeed reckons the UFO Wax Endurance Kit is good for up to 15 chains or immersions, with a single application lasting anywhere from 500 to 1,000km+ in dry conditions and 500 to 750km in the wet, all while reducing drivetrain friction losses from the 5-10 watts seen in traditional lubes (which tend to need maintenance every few hundred kilometres), to 2 to 4 watts.

These are all CeramicSpeed’s claims; all I know is my chain seems buttery smooth and the process was quite easy if you follow my simple instructions: get big glass jar, eg, gherkin jar sans gherkins, third-fill with white spirit, remove chain from bike, place in jar and shake (not so hard that the glass cracks, which I definitely didn’t do). Drain and repeat until liquid is clear. Rinse with fairy liquid water, then warm water. Dry. Heat wax beads in supplied pot in saucepan of water on stove top until wax is melted. Wait for wax to begin to nearly re-emulsify (it drips less that way) then dip chain into wax on the chain dipper tool provided and leave immersed for a few minutes. Remove, wait for wax to harden then Robert’s your mother’s brother. Honestly, I think I’ve made it sound harder than it is.

  • Check out CeramicSpeed UFO wax at ceramicspeed.com (€54)

Sidi Aeron gravel shoes

Perfectly complementing the colour palette of the Ogio Alpha, Sidi’s latest top-tier gravel shoes are joys to behold. I’ve always seen Sidi as the flagbearers for Geppetto-level cordwaining (cobblers fix shoes, cordwainers make ‘em), and the Aerons don’t disappoint in the handmade, high-quality stakes.

But unlike some Sidis of old – which were perhaps more solid and stately than tricked out performance, the materials and patterning feel super-light and super-modern, with low-density, high-strength ripstop uppers, chunky and grippy rubber forefoot, heel counters and toe caps, and a smattering of esoteric Sidi-isms.

The dials, for example, are Sidi’s own, made in aluminium with a low profile and novel flick up/down lever for tension adjustment, while the achilles section of the heel has a retention device adjusted by two little wheels to better anchor the heel in the shoe and hence aid power transfer and boost comfort. It all works, albeit the heel system is fiddly, and like all Sidis, the Aerons are made in Italy and have super-stiff carbon soles to help you win Unbound or get to the cafe stop first.

  • Check out Sidi Aeron shoes at sidi.com (£349)

Assos Equipe RS jersey and Equipe R bib shorts

Assos, let me count the ways I love you. First, your bib shorts. Oh! How they hug the bottom, buffering the buttocks, enveloping the particulars and supporting the muscles with more passion than a soccer mom at her seven year old’s league cup final. Whether in regular or long leg length (I’d say most of the UK disposition would tend towards long; regular is best reserved for the shorter, more muscular Italian), Assos’ Equipe R bib shorts are comfy as they come, with very few seams to chafe and a cut that Assos says is designed for more aggressive riding positions, which I’m all about. If I’d have wanted less aggressive I’d have bought a Dutch bike.

Then, the jersey. Not a lot you can really say about a jersey most of the time beyond the colour, but here the Equipe RS jersey gets the subtlest points right, from the laser cut sleeves replete with air-tripping ribs to make my arms more slippery than a Wye River trout, to the tight but not restrictive fit, where shoulders can expand in an aero tuck without material bunch across the chest.

Well done, Swiss scientists.

  • Check out Assos Equipe kit at assos.com (£175 jersey/£170 bib shorts)

Look over there! That’s your weekend coming to get you.

So, until next time, ta-ta for now.
